evals.query: Create a Kora Kafka publisher interface that sends String messages to a 'user-events' topic.
expected_behavior: Declares an interface (never a class) annotated with @KafkaPublisher from io.koraframework.kafka.common.annotation, whose single value() is a kafka.producer.* config path
Adds a method annotated with @Topic (the nested @KafkaPublisher.Topic) whose value is a topic config path, absolute or leading-dot relative to the publisher path
Adds the io.koraframework:kafka dependency through the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform and KafkaModule (io.koraframework.kafka.common.KafkaModule) to the @KoraApp interface
Includes the annotation-processors (Java) or symbol-processors (Kotlin) processor
Configures kafka.producer with driverProperties bootstrap.servers and a topic section with topic = "user-events"
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora packages, io.koraframework:json-module, or io.koraframework:kora-parent
Does not use field injection or a non-Kora messaging-template abstraction; uses @KafkaPublisher with constructor injection

evals.query: I need to publish a UserEvent record (userId, eventType, timestamp) to Kafka as JSON in my Kora service.
expected_behavior: Annotates the DTO with @Json from io.koraframework.json.common.annotation
Annotates the value parameter with @Json so the processor resolves the JSON Serializer<T>
Adds the io.koraframework:json-common dependency (NOT json-module, which does not exist in 2.0) and JsonModule from io.koraframework.json.common
Does not set key.serializer / value.serializer manually in driverProperties for the @Json parameter
Does not wire a reflective ObjectMapper or com.fasterxml.jackson types; relies on Kora's compile-time @Json serializer

evals.query: Add three send methods to my Kafka publisher: fire-and-forget, one that returns broker metadata synchronously, and one that is asynchronous.
expected_behavior: Declares a method returning RecordMetadata for the blocking case
Declares a method returning Future<RecordMetadata>, CompletionStage<RecordMetadata> or CompletableFuture<RecordMetadata> for the async case
States that a void return is NOT fire-and-forget: the generated $X_Impl ends every non-future signature in .get() and blocks until the broker acks, rethrowing failures as KafkaPublishException
Achieves real fire-and-forget by returning a Future and ignoring it, or by passing a Callback, rather than by declaring void
Each method is annotated with @Topic, or takes a ProducerRecord when @Topic is omitted
Does not introduce Reactor Mono/Flux, RxJava or any non-Kora async type

evals.query: I am porting a Kora 1.x service to Kora 2.0. My publisher has `CompletionStage<RecordMetadata> send(String value)`. Kora 2.0 dropped reactive and suspend contracts, so do I have to make this synchronous?
expected_behavior: Answers NO: the Kafka publisher is an exception to the 'Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous' rule and keeps its asynchronous return types
Confirms Future<RecordMetadata>, CompletionStage<RecordMetadata> and CompletableFuture<RecordMetadata> are all still accepted by the publisher processor
Confirms Kotlin suspend fun and Deferred<RecordMetadata> publisher methods are still accepted by the KSP processor
Does not rewrite the method to a blocking void or RecordMetadata return on the false premise that async was removed
Does not confuse the publisher with repositories, HTTP clients or controllers, where suspend and reactive contracts really were removed
If it mentions Kotlin suspend/Deferred, notes they need org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-jdk8 because the generated code calls kotlinx.coroutines.future.await / asDeferred

evals.query: Port this Kora 1.x publisher to 2.0: `@Topic(".topic") void send(Context ctx, String value);` — I want the request context propagated with the record.
expected_behavior: States that Context does not exist anywhere in Kora 2.0 and must be removed from the signature
Explains that the publisher processor classifies parameters by type, so an unrecognised Context parameter is treated as a PAYLOAD parameter (the key), not as metadata
Predicts the resulting failure as a missing Serializer<Context> for that parameter rather than an 'unknown annotation' or 'unsupported parameter' error
Propagates correlation data through org.apache.kafka.common.header.Headers, which is a recognised special parameter type
Does not invent a @Context annotation, a ScopedValue-based publisher parameter, or a Kora 2.0 Context replacement type

evals.query: I want to send several Kafka records atomically so they all commit or all roll back.
expected_behavior:
Declares a payload @KafkaPublisher interface and a SECOND @KafkaPublisher interface that extends TransactionalPublisher

and nothing else
Imports TransactionalPublisher from io.koraframework.kafka.common.producer
Leaves the transactional interface empty — it inherits begin(), inTx(...) and withTx(...) and must declare no send methods of its own
Sends inside inTx(...) so the transaction commits when the lambda returns and aborts when it throws
Configures the transactional section with idPrefix / maxPoolSize / maxWaitTime ONLY, and puts driverProperties on the wrapped publisher's section instead
Clarifies that a Kafka transaction is not atomic with a database write (suggests transactional outbox), and does not assume an external @Transactional bridges Kafka and the database

evals.query: Review this Kora 2.0 publisher: `@KafkaPublisher("kafka.producer.tx") public interface TxPublisher extends TransactionalPublisher<OrderPublisher>, AutoCloseable { @Topic(".topic") void send(String value); }` where OrderPublisher is a plain interface with no annotations.
expected_behavior: Flags the extra AutoCloseable supertype: a @KafkaPublisher interface must extend either nothing or exactly one TransactionalPublisher<T>

Flags the send method on the transactional interface: the processor generates the transactional impl from the type alone and never implements declared methods, so the generated $TxPublisher_Impl fails to compile as not abstract and not overriding send
Flags that the TransactionalPublisher type argument OrderPublisher must itself be annotated @KafkaPublisher
Rewrites it as an empty transactional interface extending only TransactionalPublisher<OrderPublisher>, with @KafkaPublisher added to OrderPublisher
Does not suggest annotating the transactional interface's methods, adding @Component to it, or implementing TransactionalPublisher manually

evals.query: How do I handle publish failures and serialization errors when sending to Kafka in Kora?
expected_behavior: Catches io.koraframework.kafka.common.exceptions.KafkaPublishException for blocking sends and inspects getCause()
Catches org.apache.kafka.common.errors.SerializationException for serialization failures and notes the record never reached the broker
For Future/CompletionStage signatures, handles failures via the returned handle (for example exceptionally / whenComplete)
Does not claim KafkaPublishException is thrown synchronously by async Future/CompletionStage methods
Does not wrap JsonWriter.toByteArray in try/catch (IOException)
Does not rely on a non-Kora error-handling framework; handles failures with plain try/catch and Kora exception types

evals.query: This custom Kafka serializer stopped compiling after the Kora 2.0 upgrade: `public byte[] serialize(String topic, MyEvent data) { try { return writer.toByteArray(data); } catch (IOException e) { throw new SerializationException(e); } }`
expected_behavior: Identifies the error as 'exception IOException is never thrown in body of corresponding try statement'
Explains that JsonWriter.toByteArray declares no checked exception in Kora 2.0 (the 1.x throws IOException and the *Unchecked variants are both gone)
Removes the try/catch and the java.io.IOException import, returning writer.toByteArray(data) directly
Does not replace the catch with catch (Exception e) merely to keep the old structure, and does not suggest toByteArrayUnchecked, which no longer exists
Registers the serializer as a @Component bound under a @Tag matching the publisher parameter

evals.query: I need a custom Kafka serializer for my event type instead of the default JSON one.
expected_behavior: Implements org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Serializer<T> and registers it as a @Component
Binds the serializer under a @Tag and references the same @Tag class literal on the publisher method parameter or ProducerRecord type argument
Resolves the serializer from the application graph at compile time rather than via reflection
Does not configure value.serializer as a class name string in driverProperties for the tagged parameter
Selects the serializer with @Tag rather than @Qualifier or external bean definitions

evals.query: I want to publish a Kafka record with a key, headers, and a callback in my Kora publisher.
expected_behavior: Declares a @Topic method taking value plus optional key and org.apache.kafka.common.header.Headers
Declares the ProducerRecord<K, V> method WITHOUT @Topic (the topic comes from the record) and in a SEPARATE @KafkaPublisher interface from the @Topic methods
Declares a method accepting an org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.Callback alongside the record or unpacked parameters

Explains that mixing @Topic methods and ProducerRecord methods in one interface makes the generated $X_TopicConfig record and $X_PublisherModule factory disagree on arity, so the generated code does not compile
Does not use field injection and uses constructor injection for the publisher in the caller

evals.query: Show me a Kora 2.0 Kafka publisher config that demonstrates producer metrics and logs. My current config only sets driverProperties and I see no producer meters or log lines.
expected_behavior: States that in Kora 2.0 telemetry logging.enabled and metrics.enabled both default to FALSE (only tracing.enabled defaults to true), so nothing is emitted until they are switched on
Explicitly sets kafka.producer.<name>.telemetry.logging.enabled = true and telemetry.metrics.enabled = true in the config it produces
Does not claim producer telemetry is on by default or that a missing dependency / log level is the cause
Optionally mentions metrics.driverMetrics (default false) to bind Micrometer KafkaClientMetrics to the raw producer
Names the real meters (messaging.client.operation.duration, messaging.client.sent.messages) rather than inventing kafka_producer_* metric names

evals.query: Port my Kora 1.x producer telemetry customisation to 2.0. I had a KafkaProducerLogger implementation registered through a telemetry listener factory component to change the log lines.
expected_behavior: States that the 1.x KafkaProducerLogger-style listener interfaces and their factory registration no longer exist in Kora 2.0

Replaces it by declaring a @Component that EXTENDS DefaultKafkaPublisherLoggerFactory (or DefaultKafkaPublisherMetricsFactory for meters), which KafkaPublisherModule (via KafkaModule) injects as a @Nullable dependency into the default telemetry factory
Passes the injected @Tag(KafkaPublisherTelemetry.class) MaskingStrategy to super(...) — DefaultKafkaPublisherLoggerFactory has no no-arg constructor
Mentions that replacing telemetry wholesale means a @Component implementing KafkaPublisherTelemetryFactory, which overrides the @DefaultComponent supplied by KafkaPublisherModule
Uses the io.koraframework.kafka.common.producer.telemetry package (impl subpackage for the Default* classes)
Does not invent a listener-registration API, an All<T> collection of listeners, or a config key that names a logger class

evals.query: Our Kora 2.0 Kafka publisher adds an `x-api-key` header to every record. I want producer debug logs, including the record payload, but the API key must never be logged. How do I configure this?
expected_behavior: Enables kafka.producer.<name>.telemetry.logging.enabled = true and explains that headers are logged only when the publisher's logger is at TRACE
Adds x-api-key to telemetry.logging.maskHeaders while keeping authorization, cookie and set-cookie, since the configured list replaces the default; matching is case-insensitive
States that the Kafka publisher never logs record keys or values, at any level — only masked headers — so the payload cannot be obtained from producer telemetry
Mentions that the masked value is produced by the @Tag(KafkaPublisherTelemetry.class) MaskingStrategy (default ***), replaceable with a tagged MaskingStrategy component such as MaskingKeepLast
Does not invent a producer DataMasker, a body-masking config key or a payload-logging switch for the publisher

evals.query: Write a Kotlin @KoraAppTest integration test for my Kora 2.0 Kafka publisher using Testcontainers, and give me the Gradle test dependencies.
expected_behavior: Does NOT use the Testcontainers 1.x coordinate org.testcontainers:kafka, which no longer exists in the Testcontainers 2.x line Kora 2.0 builds against
Uses org.testcontainers:testcontainers-kafka with the org.testcontainers.kafka.KafkaContainer class (or the io.goodforgod:testcontainers-extensions-kafka extension the migrated Kora examples use)
Uses @KoraAppTest with KoraAppTestConfigModifier and KoraConfigModification.ofSystemProperty(...) to feed the broker address into the HOCON substitution
Injects the publisher with @TestComponent
Notes that the publisher must be reachable from a @Root in MAIN sources or Kora prunes it, and that @KoraAppTest(components = ...) does not bring a pruned node back
Does not use org.testcontainers.containers.KafkaContainer (the removed 1.x Confluent-based class)

evals.query: In Kotlin, I want to publish two events inside one Kafka transaction from a suspend function. My publisher method is `suspend fun publish(event: MyEvent): RecordMetadata`.
expected_behavior: Keeps the suspend publisher method — it is a supported Kora 2.0 KSP publisher shape
Adds org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-jdk8 because the generated $X_Impl.kt calls kotlinx.coroutines.future.await
Uses begin().use { } for the transaction, because use is an inline function and therefore permits suspend calls in its lambda
Explains that inTx/withTx take non-inline SAM callbacks (TransactionalConsumer / TransactionalFunction), so a suspend send cannot be called from inside them
If it uses inTx for a non-suspend case, names the SAM type explicitly because inTx and withTx are each overloaded and Kotlin cannot infer the SAM from a bare lambda
Does not mark the transactional wrapper interface's inherited methods as suspend or add methods to it

evals.query: What spans and meter tags does a Kora 2.0.0.RC2 @KafkaPublisher produce when tracing and metrics are on?
expected_behavior: Names the per-record PRODUCER span 'send <topic>' (RC1 used '<topic> send') with messaging.operation.name = send and messaging.operation.type = send
Mentions the INTERNAL 'producer transaction' span for transactional publishers, with messaging.operation.name = commit or rollback

Lists messaging.client.operation.duration and messaging.client.sent.messages with messaging.system, messaging.client.id, messaging.operation.name, messaging.operation.type, destination name/partition and error.type
Says metrics.enabled defaults to false while tracing.enabled defaults to true
